milestone: from-scratch best 165.484 mm - the 166.855 lock broken by micro-legalization of the clamped-sheet ladder's rejected terminal states
attribution: rungs 0-3 (166.655, 166.488, 166.321, 166.205) and rung 7 (165.484) were published by the micro-legalization pass; rungs 4-6 (166.141, 166.074, 165.491) by the separator legalizing a target itself. The separator's own publications warm-start from the micro-legalized state carried out of rung 3, so the whole descent below the lock is downstream of the repair pass: without it the ladder publishes nothing at rungs 0-3 and enters rung 4 still holding the 166.855 parent.
mechanism: the ladder's rejected terminal states split into two residue classes. Boundary-only residues - one piece protruding past the canonical-grid sheet inset by 0.049 to 0.505 mm, no violating pair - are projected back inside by the repair pass in 7 of 8 attempts, moving one seed piece plus a two-piece one-hop neighbourhood by at most a few tenths of a millimetre. Pair residues are refused at admission: their envelopes need 0.9 to 4.3 mm of travel to come apart, which is not a rounding-scale miss.
residueFinding: the ledger's characterisation of the residue as '1-5 clearance pairs at ~0.001 mm' holds only for the boundary class. Measured per gate, the pair class misses the requested clearance by up to 5 mm and needs whole millimetres of envelope separation, because the canonical-grid envelope is miter-joined and its spikes collide far from the material closest-approach point.
note: parents produced at search allowance 0.0005 must be replayed with that allowance (CLI slot 48); at the 0.002 default they fail the canonical-grid sheet gate
